name: Epic Trailer for a Boring Errand
why_it_works: Blockbuster-trailer language applied to a tiny errand is a classic scale mismatch: the bigger the drama, the funnier the small truth. Everyone knows the feeling of putting something off, so the trailer laughs at that shared habit, and the reveal makes the brand's errand feel easy and quick by comparison.

hook.pattern: Open like a movie trailer with a grand 'In a world...' line about a small, relatable thing people put off.
examples: In a world... where nobody books {{errand}}.
This fall, one hero faces the unthinkable: {{errand}}.
They said it couldn't be done: {{errand}}.

craft.technique: Scale mismatch parody (epic trailer voice on a mundane task)
craft.notes: Setup: full blockbuster grammar (the 'In a world' line, the struggling hero, slow-motion walk) applied to a small errand; the bigger the production, the bigger the eventual drop. Turn: a hard cut to flat daylight and a deadpan line stating the real, short runtime; the deflation is the laugh and also the selling point. Tag: a parody title card with a movie-rating pun, which extends the bit one last beat. Timing: the voiceover lines are cut to a few words (the hook is only 'In a world...') so the trailer voice can leave long dramatic gaps at the ellipses and each line feels heavier; then kill the music completely on the cut to daylight and deliver the runtime with no pause. This is the one template in the comedy set that earns a clip_hero shot: the joke only works if the fake trailer looks genuinely expensive.

do_not: Shame the viewer for procrastinating; the hero is lovable and the whole audience is in on it
Imitate a real movie, studio logo, franchise or a real trailer narrator's voice
Use the clip_hero shot without the client approving the spend
Exaggerate the danger of skipping the errand into a scare tactic
compliance: Dental: frame the errand as a routine visit; no clinical claims, no 'painless' promises, and no scare tactics about what happens if you wait; results vary, so make no guarantee about the visit
Auto: if the overdue sign mentions warning lights, it is a joke, not safety advice; do not suggest it is safe to ignore real warning lights
Podcasts and sports teams: no real movie, studio, franchise, league logo or narrator sound-alike
